title: Range
description:
Write a function `range` that returns an array of numbers from `start` to `end` (inclusive) with an optional `step` (default `1`). Return an empty array when `start > end`.

**Example:**
```js
range(1, 5)    // [1, 2, 3, 4, 5]
range(0, 10, 2) // [0, 2, 4, 6, 8, 10]
range(5, 3)    // []
```
ai_context: Learners often use exclusive end (`i < end`) instead of inclusive (`i <= end`), missing the last value. Another pitfall: forgetting the default parameter for step, causing `step` to be `undefined` and the loop to produce `NaN` entries when doing arithmetic with it.
